context: Request: which Litigation (General) matters (not IP, employment or antitrust) involved a punitive or exemplary damages claim the firm actually pursued, prosecuting or defending, rather than boilerplate. Rubric: seven qualifying matters 1006-00005, 1021-00006, 1023-00002, 1024-00003, 1033-00006, 1034-00003, 1045-00004, plus a precision criterion. Documents in folder 1045-00004 carry the internal number 1022-00005.

stages.stage: List files in the document store
stages.note: Whole-store glob; the summary treats one litigation folder as the only litigation matter, and the review asks for a per-folder relisting.

stages.stage: List files in the document store
stages.note: Attempt 2: a script prints every file grouped by matter (about 809K characters). The end note says this looked like folder-listing work, and the next listing was declared that way.

stages.stage: List matter folders
stages.note: Compact list of matter numbers with file counts; the review asks how the store records practice groups.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Store-wide extraction script times out; a range-split rerun saves 1,444 hit lines to a file and per-matter counts are printed. The review flags the tail cap, the hand-picked high-confidence list and no practice-group filter, and suggests a new step to restrict hits by practice group.

stages.stage: Tabulate candidate matters from saved results
stages.note: declared: new: Restrict hits to Litigation (General) matters. A path-keyword filter over the saved hit file (about 28K characters) lists litigation-type files per matter; the summary names seven candidates. The review says the shortlist looks hand-picked and asks for a practice-group filter over the full hit list.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: declared: new: Verify practice group for all punitive-hit matters. Reads the engagement letters of the seven shortlisted matters; the review flags a matter-number mismatch inside one folder's letter and first-80-line reads.
stages.agent_new: Verify practice group for all punitive-hit matters

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: declared: new: Verify practice group for all punitive-hit matters (attempt 2). Seven reads refused because no stage was open, then the same reads (opening memo, intake form, petitions, complaints, a motion to dismiss the punitive claim), greps of the saved hits for two matters and reads of four more pleadings and a summary-judgment memo; one intake path fails.
stages.agent_new: Verify practice group for all punitive-hit matters

stages.stage: Write the response
stages.note: Writes five qualifying matters, with the folder whose documents carry another matter number named by its folder, and lists exclusions.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Re-reads the response; a path check fails on the file location, then confirms 37 cited paths exist.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Attempt 2: re-reads the opening sections of the five matters' pleadings and the opening memo; no change. The review flags the number mismatch; its end note says the calls looked like screening, and no stage follows.

stages.stage: Finish the run
stages.note: Calls finish.

runs.sequence: List files in the document store → List matter folders → Scan document text with an extraction script → Tabulate candidate matters from saved results → Screen candidate matters by reading documents → Write the response → Check or revise the response → Finish the run
runs.failure_point: It shortlisted seven of the scan-hit matters, never opened two qualifying matters that its own filter output showed, and answered with five.

first_error.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
first_error.critic_note: (generic flag) The reviews at [29] and [35] said the shortlist was hand-picked and asked for the full hit list to be filtered by practice group; the agent read only its seven shortlisted matters, and no review named the two left out.
first_error.why: Two qualifying matters appeared in its scan and filter output at [27] and [33], but it chose to read only the seven matters of its shortlist and never opened either, so the answer omits both.

stages.stage: List files in the document store
stages.note: Whole-store glob; the summary names the one litigation folder seen.

stages.stage: List files in the document store
stages.note: Attempt 2: a script prints every file grouped by matter (about 648K characters). The end note says this looked like folder-listing work; no later stage lists folders.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Store-wide extraction script times out; four parallel range reruns each time out and each print over 1.1M characters of hits (the range arguments are ignored), and the run ends without a deliverable.

runs.sequence: List files in the document store → Scan document text with an extraction script
runs.failure_point: Its parallel scan reruns printed several million characters of hits and the context filled before any reading or writing.

first_error.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
first_error.critic_note: The run ended inside the scan stage, before its stage_end review.
first_error.why: Four parallel scan reruns each returned over a million characters of hit text, which filled the context before any answer was written.

stages.stage: List files in the document store
stages.note: Whole-store glob; the review asks for a per-folder relisting.

stages.stage: List matter folders
stages.note: Matter numbers with file counts.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Store-wide extraction script times out after printing about 465K characters of hits up to mid-store.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Attempt 2: a background scan writing compact per-matter hits to a file, polled with tail and keyword filters while still running. The review flags that it never finished and that the filtered views show mostly boilerplate.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Attempt 3: stops the still-running scan and summarises 184 matter entries. The review flags unconfirmed coverage and suggests a new step to identify the practice group's matters.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: declared: new: Identify Litigation (General) matters. Seven engagement-letter reads with guessed wildcard paths; six fail and the one that opens shows a matter number different from its folder. The review flags the guessed paths.

stages.stage: List files in candidate matters
stages.note: Lists all files of 14 named candidate matters (about 42K characters).

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: Reads the opening of seven engagement letters to judge the practice group; the review flags the hand-picked 14-matter set. The start note pointed to screening for this reading work, kept under the listing label.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: Reads openings of petitions, complaints, mediation statements and motion analyses of three candidates; the review flags that only three matters were read.

stages.stage: Search within a candidate matter's files
stages.note: Snippet script over seven named candidates (about 86K characters written, part shown), a closing-document scan and an empty grep over one folder. The end note says the calls looked like listing reads; the next reads were declared as in-depth reads.

stages.stage: Read a chosen matter's documents in depth
stages.note: Reads engagement letters at offsets, two case-assessment memos, an opening memo and a motion of three candidates. The review flags the number mismatch between the folder and the matter number in its documents.

stages.stage: Write the response
stages.note: Writes seven qualifying matters, naming one by the number printed in its documents with the folder given as a storage note.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Re-reads the response; a path check fails on the file location, then 50 cited paths exist.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Attempt 2: a script confirms the punitive-damages wording in each cited pleading or motion; no change. The end note says the calls looked like scan work; no stage follows.

stages.stage: Finish the run
stages.note: Calls finish.

runs.sequence: List files in the document store → List matter folders → Scan document text with an extraction script → Screen candidate matters by reading documents → List files in candidate matters → Screen candidate matters by reading documents → Search within a candidate matter's files → Read a chosen matter's documents in depth → Write the response → Check or revise the response → Finish the run
runs.failure_point: It named one qualifying matter by the number printed inside its documents rather than its folder number, so the answer asserts a matter outside the qualifying set.

first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The review at [101] said the matter's documents carry a number different from its folder and that the agent had not resolved which number applies; it wrote the document number as the matter number with a storage note.
first_error.why: The answer names one qualifying matter by the internal matter number printed in its opening memo and engagement letter (read at [44]-[53] and [93]-[99]) rather than by the folder that holds it, so it asserts a matter number outside the qualifying set.

divergence: All fail, in three different ways. T1 overflowed the context in its first scan stage (parallel reruns each printing over a million characters). T0 and T2 both completed scans that surfaced all seven matters and then picked a shortlist: T0 shortlisted seven matters (adding an eighth later) and never opened two qualifying ones (first error at screening; the reviews flagged a hand-picked shortlist only generically); T2 shortlisted and read all seven but wrote one by the number printed in its documents instead of its folder number (first error at writing; the review had named the mismatch specifically). The agent-defined practice-group stages (T0 restrict and verify, T2 identify) did not change which matters were opened.
